comments.body:
ADR 0118 text (`docs/adr/0118-mcp-surface-derived-from-library.md`, modelled on the existing ADR form):

Title: The MCP tool surface is derived from the library facade (MCP only). Status: Accepted. Ticket: this story. Supersedes: the "no generated adapters (Pattern A)" clause of topaz-blubbery-mice (c996-8a5f-5123-4f8e), for the MCP surface only. Relates to: ADR 0100 (untouched).

Context. topaz-blubbery-mice (2026-08) built the behavioural write-parity oracle and decided not to generate the lib/CLI/MCP adapters because behaviour is single-sourced and the adapters carry irreducible hand-written value (LLM-facing docstrings, CLI ergonomics). The oracle asserts behaviour on three write ops; it cannot see shape. On 2026-09-02 lowly-lawrencium-ovenbird (3a02-66ea-9229-470c) found 41 canonical properties missing from the MCP output mirror and model defaults emitting schema-violating nulls, while the name-only parity gate (`check_mcp_library_parity.py`) had passed throughout. The MCP tools are 48 closures that call one `rebar.*` function each; three undeclared input divergences exist today (`list_tickets.priority`, `bridge_run.profile`, `transition_ticket` parameter order).

Decision. For MCP only: (1) `outputSchema`s are the canonical `src/rebar/schemas/*.json` files, inlined and advertised directly; tools return the library payload unchanged, absent keys stay absent, and the pydantic mirror is deleted. (2) The 48 library-backed tools are derived at registration from the annotated library signatures through one factory (`_mcp_derive.derive_tool`) plus an explicit override table (`_mcp_tool_specs.py`) that carries every deliberate divergence, every pinned kwarg, every per-op hook and the LLM-facing description verbatim. The 16 MCP-only tools stay hand-written. The CLI stays under ADR 0100; Pattern A remains rejected there because CLI ergonomics are not a projection of the library signature.

Consequences. One contract per shape; a schema edit changes the wire without a second edit. Divergence is declared in the override table or it does not exist; the name-only parity gate, its manifest and the model drift gate are deleted. Explicit nulls the mirror invented disappear (pre-1.0 BREAKING, recorded in release notes). LLM-facing text is pinned byte-for-byte by a golden of the live tool surface. The hand-written value the original clause protected is preserved in the table, not in code copies.

Release note for this story: none beyond the ADR reference; input schemas, descriptions and annotations are pinned byte-identical to the schema-story server by the golden file.

Experiment result (2026-09-07, scratch worktree at origin/main 4c77d6f3e96f, venv mcp 1.29.0): the golden capture in this ticket's first comment works and is stable. Three runs (same cwd; different cwd with a scratch HOME; with `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` unset) produced byte-identical JSON: 64 tools, 75,422 bytes, all 64 with annotations, 51 with an `outputSchema` and the expected 13 without, and zero matches for absolute paths, usernames, hostnames, dates, or version strings, so the golden is safe to commit.

Two corrections to the capture and the golden test that follow from it:
1. `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` does NOT change the advertised surface (it is a call-time gate inside the tool bodies, e.g. `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:282`; `build_server()` at `mcp_server.py:630-632` registers every registrar unconditionally), so the `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM=1` prefix in the capture command is inert; drop it to avoid implying a dependency.
2. `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1` DOES change the surface: 37 tools instead of 64 (the 27 write and bridge-mutation tools are not registered; the 37 shared entries are identical). The capture must run with `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` unset (`env -u REBAR_MCP_READONLY python -c ...`), and `test_live_surface_equals_golden` must `monkeypatch.delenv("REBAR_MCP_READONLY", raising=False)` before `build_server()` so a developer's shell setting cannot flip the test. compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The 48 `exact`/`co_names` MCP tools are hand-copied closures (`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py`, `_mcp_writes.py`) whose only guard is a 572-LOC introspection script (`scripts/check_mcp_library_parity.py`), a 486-LOC test and a 919-line manifest that compare names. The epic's experiment found three undeclared shape divergences it cannot see (`list_tickets.priority`, `bridge_run.profile`, `transition_ticket` parameter order). Ticket topaz-blubbery-mice (c996-8a5f-5123-4f8e) chose "no generated adapters (Pattern A)" for all three surfaces; the post-oracle escape lowly-lawrencium-ovenbird shows the MCP copy still drifts. ADR 0119 supersedes that clause for MCP only; the CLI stays under ADR 0100. Cites are on origin/main b1228deb72f (after the schema story; the comments' 083620b0 cites are superseded where they differ).

## Approach
New `src/rebar/_mcp_derive.py` (factory plus hooks, about 250 LOC) and `src/rebar/_mcp_tool_specs.py` (the override table, about 500 LOC). `ToolSpec` is a frozen dataclass: `name, library, registrar ("read"|"write"|"bridge_mutation"), annotation (preset key), description (verbatim, including the current 8-space continuation indentation so bytes are identical), strip (extra params), params (per-param annotation and default overrides), order, pins (fixed kwargs; callables evaluated per call), pre (gate hooks), post (result hooks)`. Output schemas stay in `_mcp_schema.OUTPUT_SCHEMAS_BY_TOOL` (one registry, also covering MCP-only tools), so specs carry none. The factory `derive_tool(mcp, spec, ctx)` resolves hints with `typing.get_type_hints(fn, globalns=vars(sys.modules[fn.__module__]), localns=vars(rebar.types))` (never `inspect.signature(eval_str=True)`, which raises on the `TYPE_CHECKING`-only TypedDict names); builds an `inspect.Signature` from the library parameters minus `repo_root`, `_`-prefixed names and `spec.strip`, applying `params`/`order` (VAR_POSITIONAL becomes `list[T]`); creates ONE wrapper `def tool(*args, **kwargs)` that `sig.bind`s, runs the PRE hooks, calls `getattr(rebar, spec.library)(**bound, **pins)`, runs the POST hooks in order, and sets `__name__`, `__doc__`, `__signature__`, `__annotations__`; then registers with `mcp.tool(annotations=presets[spec.annotation])(tool)`. Because `mcp.tool` is the already-layered decorator, the four existing layers attach unchanged: error guard (`_mcp_errors.py:77-133`), JS-safe guard (`:168-199`), canonical outputSchema layer (`_mcp_schema.install_canonical_output_schemas`), advisory suppression (`_lib_warn.suppress_library_double_advisory`), operation snapshot (`_operation_config.py:313`), composed in `mcp_server.py:560-589`; `functools.wraps` propagates `__signature__` through them. The named hooks, pins, the eight input overrides, and the ten declared divergences carried verbatim from the manifest are itemised in this ticket's first comment. Registration-time gating is unchanged: `register_write_tools` still returns early when `ctx.readonly()` (`_mcp_writes.py:162`) and `register_bridge_tools` registers the four bridge mutations only when not read-only (`_mcp_reads.py:136`); the 16 `mcp_only` tools remain hand-written in their registrars, so `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` grouping and output are unchanged; `_mcp_inflight` and `_cap_workflow_payload` are consumed only by `mcp_only` tools (`_mcp_llm.py:14`, `get_workflow_*`) and stay where they are. Delete the parity script, its test, the manifest, `Makefile:298-310`, the stub at `tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py:319`, and the manifest row at `docs/generated-artifacts.md:39` (adding the golden's row). Write `docs/adr/0119-mcp-surface-derived-from-library.md` (text in the second comment; 0118 is now taken by adaptive-snapshot-cadence, so this is the next free number) with `docs/adr/.numbers/0119`, index it in `docs/adr/README.md`, and describe the derivation and override table in `docs/architecture.md`'s MCP section.

## Scope
New: `src/rebar/_mcp_derive.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_tool_specs.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/mcp_tool_surface_golden.json`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_tool_surface_golden.py`, `docs/adr/0119-mcp-surface-derived-from-library.md`, `docs/adr/.numbers/0119`. Delete: `scripts/check_mcp_library_parity.py`, `tests/unit/test_mcp_library_parity.py`, `tests/unit/mcp_library_parity_manifest.json`. Edit: `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`, `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` (`--update-stale`), `Makefile`, `tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py`, `docs/generated-artifacts.md`, `docs/adr/README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/release-notes.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Also edit `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp.py` (its core-only fallback test now loads `_mcp_tool_specs`, where the TypedDict rebuild moves) and `tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py` (its source scan for `rebar.comment(ticket_id, body)` becomes an assertion on the derived `comment_ticket` signature). Kept unchanged: `tests/interfaces/facades/test_parity.py`, `tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py`, `write_parity_contract.py`, `adapters.py`, `.github/complexity-baseline.json` (`register_read_tools`/`register_write_tools` lose nested defs and bucket `stale`, which passes). Out of scope: the 16 MCP-only tools, the CLI, the library signatures.

## Testing
Golden capture, run once from the schema story's landed tree before writing any derivation code, with the SHA recorded in the test docstring (command in the first comment) producing `tests/interfaces/facades/mcp_tool_surface_golden.json` with `inputSchema`, `description`, and `annotations` for all 64 tools. `test_mcp_tool_surface_golden.py`: `test_live_surface_equals_golden` parametrized over the 64 golden names (dict comparison; `required` lists compared as lists); `test_golden_covers_exactly_the_live_tools` (set equality both ways); `test_every_derived_tool_names_a_public_library_symbol` (each spec's `library` is in `rebar.__all__`); `test_stripped_params_are_only_repo_root_private_or_declared` (a spec may strip only `repo_root`, `_*`, or a name listed in its `divergence` note). Behavioural suites pass unchanged: `tests/interfaces/facades/test_parity.py`, `tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py`, `tests/unit/test_cross_session_mcp.py`, `test_mcp_writes.py`, `test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py`, `test_mcp_output_schema_canonical.py`. `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py --check`, `python scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`, `make verify`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For all 64 tools, `list_tools()` `inputSchema`, `description`, and `annotations` equal the committed golden (the golden test).
- [ ] `_mcp_reads.py` and `_mcp_writes.py` contain `def` bodies only for the 16 `mcp_only` tools plus registrars and helpers; `grep -c "@mcp.tool" src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` reports 8 and 1.
- [ ] `scripts/check_mcp_library_parity.py`, `tests/unit/test_mcp_library_parity.py`, and the manifest are gone and `make lint` no longer invokes the script (grep and `make -n lint`).
- [ ] The behavioural parity suites named above pass without modification (`git diff --stat` on those paths is empty).
- [ ] `docs/mcp-reference.md` is unchanged (`--check`); ADR 0119 passes `check_adr_numbers.py` and is indexed (CI).
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0; the complexity ratchet reports only `stale`; the mechanism ratchet reports `new=0` after `--update-stale` for the removed `scripts/check_*.py` gate.
